# Task list

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a task list to show the tasks in a multi-part service and help users understand which are complete or still need attention.

## When to use

- Use for services with several tasks that users may complete over time or in a flexible order.
- Show a clear current status for each task and link only tasks the user can open.

## When not to use

- Do not use for a short linear journey where normal page navigation is clearer.
- Do not use as a generic navigation menu or checklist unrelated to completing a service.

## Anatomy

- **Task list (required):** A govuk-task-list ul contains one li per task.
- **Task name and hint (required):** The task has a concise name, optional hint and an href only when it is available.
- **Status (required):** A uniquely identified status is referenced from the task link using aria-describedby.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linked task | `li` | `govuk-task-list__item`, `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` | A task the user can currently open. |
| Unlinked task | `li` | `govuk-task-list__item` | A task that is unavailable or does not have a destination. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required; links navigate to the corresponding task.
- Derive status from authoritative service data and update it after task completion.
- Do not make the status itself the only clickable target when the task name is the destination.

## Accessibility contract

- Associate each link with its unique status ID using aria-describedby.
- Status text must be meaningful without its tag colour.
- Keep list order and task availability understandable to keyboard and screen-reader users.

## Content rules

- Name each task with a concise verb phrase or recognisable subject.
- Use a small consistent status vocabulary, such as “Not started”, “In progress” and “Completed”.
- Add hint text only when the task name does not provide enough context.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

## HTML examples

### One task with status

```html
<ul class="govuk-task-list">
  <li class="govuk-task-list__item govuk-task-list__item--with-link">
    <div class="govuk-task-list__name-and-hint"><a class="govuk-link govuk-task-list__link" href="/company-details" aria-describedby="company-details-status">Company details</a></div>
    <div class="govuk-task-list__status" id="company-details-status">Completed</div>
  </li>
</ul>
```
